identity.title: CodeIO: Condensing Reasoning Patterns via Code Input-Output Prediction

problem.claim: Improve reasoning across diverse tasks beyond narrow math or code-generation skills.

gap.claim: Progress on many reasoning tasks is limited by sparse and fragmented training data.

contributions.claim: CodeI/O systematically converts contextually grounded code into code input-output prediction formats to condense diverse reasoning patterns.
It trains models to predict code inputs and outputs in natural-language CoT rationales, exposing general reasoning primitives while decoupling structured reasoning from code syntax.
CodeI/O++ verifies predictions through ground-truth matching or code re-execution and uses multi-turn revision to enhance CoTs.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors describe CodeI/O as a novel approach for systematically condensing reasoning patterns embedded in contextual code.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report consistent improvements across symbolic, scientific, logic, math and numerical, and commonsense reasoning tasks.
The authors report that CodeI/O++ achieves higher performance after prediction verification and multi-turn CoT revision.

narrative_sequence.summary: The abstract identifies broad reasoning improvement as difficult when training data are sparse and fragmented outside narrow skills.
CodeI/O transforms original code into input-output prediction tasks to condense diverse reasoning patterns.
Natural-language CoT prediction exposes planning, search, traversal, and decomposition while preserving procedural structure without code-specific syntax.
The authors report cross-domain gains, then introduce verified, revised CoTs in CodeI/O++ with higher reported performance.

source_observation.claim: The abstract explicitly links the representation change—code to natural-language input-output prediction—to several named reasoning primitives and then reports gains across varied task families.

lessons.interpretation: A representation can make the intended transferable reasoning structure explicit while reducing dependence on domain-specific surface form.
lessons.application: When proposing a cross-task reasoning method, map the training representation to named reasoning operations and evaluate it across multiple task families.
lessons.exception: This framing may be unsuitable when performance depends essentially on exact domain syntax or when broad cross-task evaluation is unavailable.

unknowns: The abstract does not provide metrics, dataset sizes, baselines, statistical variation, or task-by-task results.
It does not specify how prediction verification and multi-turn revision are implemented or how much each contributes.
Public availability is promised, but release timing and exact contents are unspecified.
